deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 57-59, Jan. 1983): Grothendieck is studying a configuration space 𝒳 attached to a system of n pseudo-lines in the projective plane. This is the space of 'positions' of an additional pseudo-line D relative to the system, together with a covering 𝒳~ and a part 𝒳^ess. Parallel transport of a position along a loop permutes the 2n cyclically ordered 'ends' or polygon vertices of Pol(D). This gives a monodromy homomorphism π1(𝒳) → D_{2n}, the dihedral group acting on Z/2n. Composing with the orientation character χ: D_{2n} → ±1 records whether the orientation of the position is preserved.

On the previous page he showed that the image of π1(𝒳~) contains the rotation subgroup Z/n. He uses the rotations t ↦ t-(n-1) and t ↦ t-2(n-1) and gcd arguments. So the image has index dividing 4, with quotient D_2 ≅ F2×F2. What remains is the image in ±1. His plan is to rotate a pseudo-line half a turn about a vertex s of the arrangement. The half-turn sends (D_i^s, ω) to (D_i^s, -ω), and the loop is closed via the orientation reversal. χ of the loop is +1 if the number of elementary moves ('pas') is odd and -1 if it is even.

This page:
(1) He announces that a modification of the procedure will show surjectivity of π1(𝒳) → ±1 and even of π1(𝒳~) → ±1. Hence, for n even, π1(𝒳^ess) → D_{2n} is surjective, since the second factor of the D_2 quotient is detected by χ. He asks whether π1(𝒳~) → D_{2n} might fail to be surjective.
(2) First parity count of elementary operations for the half-turn:
  2·(number of 'biligne' vertices)
  + 2·(number of lines passed over while 'bilignant'; each counts like a last vertex)
  + 1 (take-off) + 1 (landing).
  This is always even ('merveilleux, c'est toujours pair!').
(3) He then sees that the argument is not correct as stated. One must work in the covering of 𝒳 quotiented by the non-pseudo-geodesic moves, which have order 2(n-1), not 2n. Better to start from a position close to D_i through s, obtained by a small rotation about s. Then each line crossed counts as a single operation, crossed exactly once. The count becomes 2·(number of multiline vertices on s) + ord(s).
(4) So the half-turn loop maps to -1 or +1 according as the index ν(s), the number of lines through s, is even or odd. A simple vertex (two lines) gives an even count, hence -1. So if the arrangement has at least one simple vertex, π1(𝒳~) → ±1 and π1(𝒳) → ±1 are surjective.

The whole page is struck through with one diagonal line. The next page redoes the argument with full turns and a comparison between Pol(D)-transport and 'ordinary' transport, concluding again that π1(𝒳) → D_{2n} is surjective.
errors: Grothendieck himself flags the first count (always even) as flawed. Non-pseudo-geodesic moves have order 2(n-1), not 2n, so one must pass to a quotient covering and restart from a nearby position. The corrected count depends on the parity of ord(s).

The surjectivity conclusion needs a vertex of even multiplicity, e.g. a simple vertex. The page states this only for simple vertices. Arrangements with all vertices of odd multiplicity are not treated here. (Every non-trivial projective arrangement has simple points? For straight lines this is Sylvester–Gallai/Melchior; for pseudo-lines it holds by Kelly–Moser/Levi-type results, but it is not invoked.)

The step 'n even ⇒ π1(𝒳^ess) → D_{2n} surjective' is asserted without detail. It requires that the image of π1(𝒳)/π1(𝒳~) and χ together hit both factors of D_2. The page was abandoned and superseded by p.59.

ideas.what: Monodromy representation of the fundamental group of the space of positions of an extra pseudo-line (relative to an arrangement) into the dihedral group D_{2n}, with orientation character
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group / monodromy of the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (one-element extensions), acting on the cyclic order of crossings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Extension spaces: Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993); pseudoline arrangements: Levi (1926), Ringel (1956), Goodman–Pollack
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; pseudo-line systems possibly alluded to only in passing in 1984 texts (unsure)

ideas.what: Parity counting of elementary moves (crossing a vertex/line, take-off, landing) along a half-turn about a vertex to compute the orientation character
ideas.modern_name: sign of a loop in the flip/mutation graph; parity of mutations (Ringel moves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (mutations connect arrangements); parity arguments folklore

ideas.what: Surjectivity of π1 → ±1 whenever the arrangement has a vertex of even multiplicity (e.g. a simple vertex)
ideas.modern_name: non-orientability / non-trivial w1 of a component of the extension space

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats the space of positions of an extra pseudo-line as a topological object with a dihedral monodromy representation and orientation character. In modern terms this is the topology (π1, orientation cover) of the one-element extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid. That topic was studied later (Sturmfels–Ziegler, Mnëv–Ziegler) mostly for connectivity and homotopy type, not via dihedral monodromy.
missed.quote: on montrera alors que non seulement π1(𝒳) → ±1, mais aussi π1(𝒳~) → ±1 est surjectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives an explicit invariant (image of π1 in D_{2n}, dependence on vertex multiplicities ν(s)) for extension spaces / spaces of pseudo-line positions, a viewpoint possibly absent from the oriented-matroid literature.

missed.claim: Open question whether π1(𝒳~) → D_{2n} (as opposed to 𝒳^ess) is surjective, and the case n odd. Neither is settled on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A concrete combinatorial-topological question about pseudo-line configuration spaces; minor.

deep.surprise_reason: A struck-out, self-corrected parity computation within an unpublished study of pseudo-line arrangements. The overall programme (topology/monodromy of pseudo-line position spaces) is little known, but this page itself is a routine, superseded step.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 'par contre [?] dans le cas' is more likely 'je dis dans le cas n pair, cela implique que π1(𝒳^ess) → D_{2n} est surjectif'.
Final lines: 'π1(𝒳^{?}) → ±1' is π1(𝒳~) → ±1 (tilde visible), followed by 'et aussi π1(𝒳) → ±1 surj.'
'2(nb de sommets multilignes en s)' may read 'multilignes sur s'.
The NB margin reads roughly: 'NB chaque droite par dessus laquelle on bilignise compte comme un dernier sommet par lequel on bilignise'.
